Tryskiai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšiai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Tryskiai's Jewish community, formed in the mid-19th century, relied heavily on the tanning trade and reached 681 people (34 percent of the town) by 1897; by 1931, all 13 of the town's shops were Jewish-owned. Graduates of the local Tarbut Hebrew school often continued their studies at the Telz Yeshiva, documented elsewhere in this collection. The town's synagogues burned in numerous fires over the years, leaving even the total number that once existed uncertain. In July 1941, Tryskiai's Jewish men were marched to a nearby forest and murdered; two weeks later, women and children were taken to the Žagarė ghetto and, on October 2, 1941, shot in the city park together with 3,000 Jews from Žagarė and the surrounding towns.
